messages.author: e54c74980a01d9ed
messages.subject: Landscape covariates being read as categorical value instead of numeric
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently trying to model occupancy as a function of a variety of landscape covariates I have calculated (ex. % forest cover, %agriculture, %developed land, etc. within an eight kilometer cell displayed in excel as a value from 0-1). However, R is reading these values as a categorical value instead of as numeric. Therefore, I keep getting an error when I am running my code. Here is a short example of how I have my data formatted in excel with "develop" as % developed land within that grid cell:

grid_id   Location   Occasion1   Occasion2   Occasion3   Occasion4   develop
AL-41   414              0                    0                    0                   0                    0.023256
AL-42   366              0                    0                    1                   0                    0.022222
AM-40  166              1                   0                     0                   1                    0.021739

Here is the code I have been using:

data <- read.csv("Model_Covariates.csv")
data

y <- data[ ,3:6] #these are the camera events weeks 1-4
siteCovs <- data[,7:13] #land cover

umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, siteCovs = siteCovs)
summary(umf)

umf@siteCovs$develop <- scale(umf@siteCovs$develop)

After running the last line, I keep getting this error:
> Error in colMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric

I know this has something to do with how my data is written, but I cannot figure out how to fix this issue. Any help would be great!

Thanks!
Maria

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Landscape covariates being read as categorical value instead of numeric
parts:
Looks like R is not recognizing the missing values in your CSV ("#N/A") and thinks they are character strings, and thus turns the whole column into character. You could make those cells blank, or make them NA instead of #N/A and they should be read in correctly and keep the column numeric. You could also try setting the na.strings argument of read.csv() to explicitly tell R what values should be considered missing.

Ken
